title: Energy shock meets AI jitters: a week of falling stocks and rising yields
dek: Oil near $110 Brent, US inflation back above 4%, chip shares in retreat and France's bond market under strain — markets slid into a fearful mood.

mood.label: Nervous
mood.explanation: The VIX — Wall Street's gauge of expected swings in the S&P 500 — closed at 18.69 on 19 October, up almost 23% in a week, while CNN's Fear & Greed index fell to 20 ("extreme fear") from 46 a week earlier. Reddit chatter doubled on broad index trackers and clustered around semiconductor and AI-infrastructure names, a sign retail attention has shifted from buying dips to watching them.

regions.headline: Inflation back above 4% as the AI trade wobbles
regions.summary: September CPI rose to 4.02% year on year from 3.71% in August, driven by energy, while core inflation was broadly flat at 2.79%. The Nasdaq fell 4.48% over the week as chip and AI-linked shares sold off, and the 10-year Treasury yield ended Friday at 5.10%. Thirty-year mortgages were quoted at 7.40% on 15 October, keeping housing costs high.

regions.headline: France's budget crisis spills into bonds and the euro
regions.summary: Violent protests and a budget deadlock pushed French government bond yields higher and hit Paris-listed shares, with the Bank of France governor saying conditions are not met for ECB intervention. Euro area inflation was 3.75% in September, up from 3.23% in August, with the ECB's deposit rate at 2.50% before its 29 October decision. The FTSE 100 was the exception, up 1.13% on the week.

regions.headline: China grows 4.5% on exports; Korean and Japanese stocks slide
regions.summary: China's economy expanded 4.5% in the third quarter, powered by an export surge while domestic demand stayed weak. The KOSPI fell 9.65% over the week and the Nikkei 5.96% as the global semiconductor sell-off hit Asia hardest; the yen was at 158.26 per dollar. India's Sensex rose 2.68% even as September inflation neared the RBI's tolerance ceiling.

body:
## The week in one paragraph

Two forces squeezed markets at once. Energy prices jumped after Iran's Revolutionary Guard said [two tankers caught fire having struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitAFBVV95cUxQcEhpeXZhQ20xWmZjb3p1eUJRVEFVSi1QbWJnUFZpRE05QmJUd0hhMU9OQmlqMmxPemhUTGN3ZmF5YlU0LUxkaF85M2JEVEpRT1FaMVAzaV8xNTBNeGk1YUlIRVNzRFNQVkpfY3FwWllQeWU3Mmk0NEpVaV90Tkp2ZnRzQ2xaZzQ2OGRLbUp1dUVNenlPUFVuQUVGRUVKSUZRbDVVR3hjZElfSFNONWhieWF5S0_SAboBQVVfeXFMT2UzSjBRSnAybzdRcU9NRWpyV0V5SU4xT1g2LWlTNWlraWJDeFBMSDlSbGVNc093MmJCOTROSjQ5bE50Uk1WSVVMNDZGN2VRWVkyRjdFdmV3QzliaGtBci1FcjRTbll0UmZQZmJTT0tXR05oVGdjRlU3Z1FvcTNUWXVPY0drS1BvamFZdWkyU0w0QU5oSjAwTnFBU0hNc2Z6dC1yUk1ma0dDNGpZX2RuVmxEZzhrUUI4bHhn?oc=5), the narrow waterway most Gulf oil passes through; WTI crude closed at $98.37 on Monday, up 4.94% on the week, with Brent at $108.63. At the same time the year-long enthusiasm for artificial intelligence cracked, with [chip stocks caught in a global rout over AI funding worries](https://news.google.?oc=5). The S&P 500 ended Friday at 7,659.44, down 1.95% on the week; the Nasdaq Composite fell 4.48% and the Russell 2000 of smaller US companies 3.05%. Meanwhile France's budget crisis moved from politics into its bond market. The result: higher fuel bills, higher borrowing costs and a distinctly jumpy mood.

## United States

Inflation went the wrong way. September CPI rose 4.02% from a year earlier, up from 3.71% in August — [driven by surging gasoline prices](https://news.google.?oc=5) — while core CPI, which strips out food and energy, was little changed at 2.79%. Wholesale prices also [hit levels not seen since 2022](https://news.google.?oc=5). Retail sales rose 0.8% in September, though [a big chunk of that went on filling up the tank](https://news.google.?oc=5).

The labour market is softening slowly: unemployment was 4.2% in September against 4.1% in August, and [job growth cooled](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMid0FVX3lxTE8tXzZZMWJ0bEJQTWtSbmtWeFpSWWFwdHJhV05ZaW1WY1pXeldrcl9uZks1cmdRTWtScnY2RzhWdFRKWGk4Y0Y4S2xpSF9YVnJ4TTRyTmpMRkpEQlVZQXJhOE9rdklCUVFfc2x6cWJBckdJLVBrbmY4?oc=5). That combination — rising prices, cooling hiring — is awkward for the Fed, whose policy rate averaged 3.75% in September. The debate has flipped from cuts to hikes: Governor Mary Daly told Reuters that [rate hikes are likely needed but not urgently](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqAFBVV95cUxOMndHODQzSE53STRuTnVib1hVbS02ZEtKUEFmQnlqNDRFTXVHSVRxMFh1YU9IN0lLRTlPbEZsOXhHQllMczhyQ0llSHFoX3RuQTdHNUMtQUszZlZEcWJYMDRjMDAxNG5hUGNxMXZHejlZbFg5STlZekM0Vy1VeldsVGdvRXU5SVZmZTAyVTRkT0NZOHptamRHMFVqdzdBUmNONTV2eWJzaXc?oc=5), and Chair Kevin Warsh [gave no hint on the October decision](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMifkFVX3lxTFBCemtOd0VDSVprMHZTWlUwZXp4TzhkbndDVU9MTjBDeTNHMjFEQ21QM3lMdWwyYUM2dHVGanFHMjBxSElpU2FJVVlDV2hqRnlRNU5IZ2ZKSlZ5VlQyUDdyNTRCS3pKQWxSMDBKSThYUTF5Wk9pWk0wOU0zSS1hQQ?oc=5) while [praising US resilience and warning of a "bumpy" AI road ahead](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitAFBVV95cUxQQ2Z3My1DbzhJTkZzNjU4ZVg0OTA1LTZZNGNkWW9pNEhOUnI4dE90ZHg5aEZGWHBiY1RSNTlub1VNUExNclVxQVdsWmZOQ0laVmRtejdBSDYwZkgzdS1iRW1aTFZfS1QwdEEybm1vNGVyclMyUW84TTNVcDVhcXlIZHlST0NOazRkZ1kycXRRZURWVVgtaWRsUXlmbVRBaDJLanAxWDNNb0pUWUpzckhJa2pQNUg?oc=5).

For households and firms, the practical numbers are blunt. The 30-year mortgage was quoted at 7.40% on 15 October. The 10-year Treasury yield — the benchmark for long-term borrowing costs — was 5.10% on Friday, down from 5.19% midweek as money moved into bonds. The gap between 10-year and 2-year yields (the "yield curve", a rough gauge of growth expectations) was 0.35 percentage points on 16 October, still positive.

## Euro area

France is the story. Violent protests and an unresolved budget [pushed French government bond yields higher](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijwFBVV95cUxOSk1wWWp6WG1vZjdfYjZXX1hRU0lPVEl6WnVGbkozSXB5eTU5UHN2aG9nRHRpc1VMNlI5eF92YXNZNTFUOGFBMnk1anY0cUxFcG5YTTF0NFRhaGZ0VjkwbjNETmpiWkVXUHlNMmZJV014MlJ2LXRKZWlmS3E1N21wZHdnUXZybnJBRzlVSmdwUQ?oc=5) and [dragged Paris-listed shares, bonds and the euro lower](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMifEFVX3lxTE4yZ0RIWVU0dGdFR3VzT185QnhqcGFWRnZNZTlneWpIaUhVMlFqeF9pQmEtZm9SVE1GVnRMYVpiM2QwQm42QjZhUXp0ZGZhbnU2dm91TnlXWjNDbVlVNkdHQ2xic0VVTEo0aFNGWTBTZFRPYXZWMXF0VDlrWXU?oc=5). Yields on French ten-year debt averaged 4.48% in September, above Italy's 3.99% in August and Germany's 3.47% in September — an unusual ranking that tells you where investors see the risk. The Bank of France governor said conditions are [not met for ECB intervention in French bonds](https://news.google.?oc=5) while arguing France can [cut its deficit to 3% within three years](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMif0FVX3lxTE1HbUR6MnJiNFVRU0EtUlZkeWZXS2dkNF9lVzJQVjJ6dkFoT0ZsSHFTNmQ3SVljNFRKYXlYaC02QVRZV3BQRkoxVjJaV1FVQy1MNWNHQlQxWUowZk5ndWxuMTN1SHR3SGwwNEhDWEE0OGZERUFfR2dESlJpZ3kzMnM?oc=5).

Euro area inflation was 3.75% in September, up sharply from 3.23% in August, with the deposit rate at 2.50%. Christine Lagarde argued the [bond sell-off itself will slow inflation](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipgFBVV95cUxORnNpbWFQTVJFZTQ1NDEzNVA1QlMyNThGdl8tR19Bd0UtQTAyVnBGRFBldDVOMFFnRHR0WkRHaS1CODVMSUFvSTZJdzN5a2NSbHFLbHA2bnZ0ZVBXYUprYS1oeGN6eF9lakVpVmRTSVB6VkpwUzlOVXZCME5ldGVmNmZPTUtuSGVnRTZzbENrQ1pGcFlScVZ1Sl9rQ1pHWUo1c1l4VUJn?oc=5) — tighter financial conditions do some of the central bank's work. Growth is modest (1.16% year on year in Q2) and unemployment steady at 6.4% in August. Indices diverged: the DAX and CAC 40 were flat on the week, the IBEX fell 1.3% and the FTSE 100 rose 1.13% as [UK investors sheltered in defensive sectors](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqgFBVV95cUxNT3BFWnRxRUNjVFNRUVVYVER4b0o3OF84NTVXVmVmVWJMMTdwMDBLYVFBLWFvZU9fc21wMUNzb0s5R0VHLTBKS21tT2lDQkJreG1OWll6SHd6RFJ0VzhmcHB2NkFUUUVrbFkxWjU5WUNXOVVVdEJNT2lIV1JWdngtbnFNOUhncGFOczZfSU5DSko2ME5yNUlsR0hRUXJDMy04dTZjOGZZeXNUdw?oc=5).

## Asia

China's economy [grew 4.5% in the third quarter, beating estimates as exports surged](https://news.google.?oc=5), helped by [an AI-related export boom that offset domestic weakness](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiW0FVX3lxTFBKZDdHVkpOendSakJEYTM3TW1fY1JQS3BpYnZkSmtiRDJEdDlyNWZzcmFTclR6WEp5S1VtUS1ZZ0g5aE15YS14c0dsZnc4Z052M1hPZjJha0hWclk?oc=5). Consumers remain the soft spot: [exports boomed while consumers balked](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitAFBVV95cUxPelFIVGVwcy1oY2RvRVlaQTl5REpEc1hfS0ZUb1lTeWN0M2tBbTctTWo4NzVXeWthQVNab2p1eUFYQ2xtejBoc1ktQlZFQXh1U3hOSWdNdlBzTzNvcThPMFVyNnIzSTgyQ3lXbW8taGQtTV92Vl9uUGZOWjc1cGp6NTJBTDNpcWpEUnRCMjhXcVRYNkVXSFNwaHF3UGFGU0NqZTZWZzJXc0FyX3BnUkxhVWVSNzI?oc=5), and Fortune noted the export surge [risks being "a drag on world growth"](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMibEFVX3lxTFBBV2Vqam8wSnlkWWgzSlVfc21XZmJndFFZZzRyVmhUcjlPc1FhNjRWME1kajFSV1hCZzM1OHUtTEFKVXY2WlBiVGJ1bmZ5V2FHb2hnRThPX0JIODY1U2dsZTNucnZuTFdnSjJodg?oc=5) if it displaces output elsewhere. The Shanghai Composite still fell 1.75% on the week.

Korea took the brunt of the chip sell-off: the KOSPI fell 9.65% over the week after [tumbling 8% in a single session](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiswFBVV95cUxNS1ZmX19fclBFd1I3bEdCWVk5NEpfRmJGWE1VbjhDRThlVUFFeFBqYzYzTXpTR2wzeHNUcWtNN1VFV2ltaC1WNnc1S1ZsOFMxalVER01yS0otb2VjbTQ1cHJjZERsa05rMHNabDVyenp5MUlLNmpZQzdERzVzbElnTlgtQ0ljV1hsOGJNTEMwNEFPUmMtSXdjUzE3b0REWmR0ZDNfQzh0RU5UalY1dWg3b1pwVQ?oc=5) and [closing at a six-month low](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxOdWpRSjBjZzFURGRKR0VQWHlfRGlueEl6akRuam5yVExaVDJQWVYyckVBTDJ0WTlKc1F0THBUNWJBajN3bzRGa2U3TjBUSGxKS05NclZpWU14N2FVUzFoX05pQ1NwV2QtaXljRnJiUTZOc0RIaXZnMHlhX05aNmMwRmJhMmtINmRranYyVEFITFZJWnNGWFY1N2pNcEx0V3lEdTJZZWwzZnc1Y0U2ZFVpU0NnaUxydw?oc=5). Japan's Nikkei fell 5.96%, with the yen at 158.26 per dollar. Prime Minister Takaichi [denied she is driving a weak yen and high rates](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxNWnJXRW1KdHVsRVB2dzNsRDJGRk44cDJydFh0VVlvLTNwS1hGelI5Nklhajdla2M4THJVMm9YZlBMQ1NSbHYxQVduWmpoRk5sLVpVeDNFSUQ1UWozM25adGl6TTlJb1M4bkNFcFlQa3dMRUJWY0hhX1FjVzBuRnZ4LXZpcThNNFZ0N09jTk14Q0pnZGIzTk92RVJSa01kTkxobnBJYzc2SVM5MDRSbV8w?oc=5) and said bond issuance will be kept [at an appropriate level](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuAFBVV95cUxOZ2lKR2ZxaUU2WE1Zbm5GcmZINEk5OHd6Q1Vsek1tbk9lbzZ5Q2EyeDBFMXhLNGN5aktlUC1GSjJoWkU0bWJTOTRBOFlFdXhkVzRtMFh4WnpyeFJZWDBvV0tKZGVLQk5qeEVfdXNER1paT09UNnNydVNTOG5NZ2pIdmp2RFMxQklObzRhOENKaDFNSGFWNDc5VFkzTk85ZWs0MWd0djRscE0yRll5SjFhcG5MZmgzT0Jq?oc=5); her support rate [fell below 50%](https://news.google.?oc=5). The BOJ chief said underlying inflation is ["quite close" to the price goal](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinwFBVV95cUxOYWgzQmZjay1udU8wTUszWE1kX0lSeUVNa1h2YjhRV3Ztel9SMGUwdFdiTWdYTDVCVFV1STZ6QXUxZ0VpU1lxbGdQOXRlal9yZ2hDd0lJLXpfbGlQX1ZGWlh3Q0ZwTGd6aVVoSmtXWVhUYkoxd3EzeFdTem9nTDlVaUlkR1lUdjY0S044NnRJWTNIdU1BeWZaYTRPTzYzWVU?oc=5). In India, September inflation [neared the RBI's tolerance ceiling](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimAFBVV95cUxOM2hyc2tfZ1c4OFc2WGEwN3J5Ri1jaWVLOWtWbmpYTzlMcnNyVVhrN0pEdGg1ZXlKdEJMRjNiNXpRRC1KVDNXaWdDQ0ptQ245VEJaY19RZVNMUGJDYTJjUGNwV2NrLTU0LTRVbEcwWGZmSzhoX3hEdkVGcHAzTGZLb285UTBwYXhxZTVSWmxRNkt3X2xISDZwZg?oc=5), yet the Sensex rose 2.68% as the [rupee extended a winning streak](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwAFBVV95cUxNaGR1OENJajFoN1pyejk2WXpNSHBSRTFpMzl1WXFiT2NIWGloV1lPc1BkY0VCRGM0VjVrSHMzYnBNVE93WjBWSXVCcTcxVkVDRkEwMC1mUWJYeXIyUlNoMUJBV0JVWEFOaUMwV2tpOHkyVFFESTdVeDFTbnFiVTZLRHVLNVhrelFOTTdhRG5WRVJwb0RjTWF1aU9iWmRRSThRX1NzeUZQMzl5aGV1MXJjYVZrX05mb3dsRE04OGJkRUQ?oc=5).

## Debt and politics

The US federal deficit [grew to nearly $2 trillion, the highest since 2021](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxQX0FRcVdocU9ia1FaNEQxc0FJLTFRWjZKbDFmYkgtVUJsYnB1OFh2UGRQcFBpRklTMVdONmRVTFlzZ2dLNjJWTmUyRTRIX29MeVVhOGFiY3ZobFFpenI2bVd0X0VrY2FUeXB0NTJDY3ZsM0xoRkFZS2kxaVplZGNTQV9yQl92d0JHVG01TG8yR3ljQmhEOVZ1dkZUaTFySlphOEt5Z0Q1SlVCQi1Kd0gw?oc=5), with federal debt at 122.6% of GDP in Q1. Affordability is now an election issue: [wholesale inflation keeps it in focus ahead of the midterms](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilwFBVV95cUxPSGRRU3lQTklWaXR1b1FkVVZXWDFNVEZmbkhYTHhodVV1WlNZQ01XX196RVVRYnVLZVkwUVhzOUdyaE9CMXVVR3UxSnM3X1liWkF0UW40R29kZ3V0RjlKbER4UlhDM0lJcGVRMDRPb1BQbHB4OU01SW55RkotNGlTZTYtTFI0alJMNjE1aUJuRnZXWHpfYmxj?oc=5), and [key voters told a Guardian poll the economy is getting worse](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilAFBVV95cUxOSzZUX3puSnV6Q1E5OGE0SGtObWtXcTE2XzFPRTNwQ3Q1X2NkTnRrWUZwVW5PRVk0MkxIblBRM3pKN0lWZWhEalFITlNTcmlOeUh3SFFieGZtNHdqVDdneElFSnFpV0h6b3MwaXBwYTJBcG54S1ZXSWwwaHFNR0wyTWtLeG9xMWtwZlZBa1FZY3hROUot?oc=5). Social Security's cost-of-living rise of 3.6% [may finally match inflation](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijAFBVV95cUxQUjd6RWRIUGtNRS1TR29UZWZPMllRa0xFMndkOE9fS1JFWGlfTlpuYnloNnFuOVJnZmE3QkVMWWdOaHNucTgxOGVhc09yaVpMUDAzVHFvNW0zemVyMHhnV2hqNHNSOXNuUkF1RDNHVUl2Yk1MZHNicV9yVE9xWE14bDFmQmlCdWo2UHVYOA?oc=5). In Europe, government debt was 88.9% of euro-area GDP in Q1, and France's turmoil — with [Macron pointing to security failings](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipwFBVV95cUxObFBiSHhMOGNoV0YwYU9VWnhtd19tSWJCX2lrYWltV1dPMmplTmtrTzQ2cklHYk4xZjQtVkRxWDFUUEFNYlYyMmxicnMwNFpFLURhZUVQSGdwLWlQcHJZbmFiSG9YMTloRWNGa0FxcG9vX0RyRUxpeURHUWlKcGgxajdPV3RjbS12YjBxTzVkQjU1OU5BeHFFYUk0cnY1U1hEczdLQnFNWQ?oc=5) — is the clearest example of how street politics becomes a funding cost. Bloomberg reported that the bond market's big short bet [got a wake-up call as the AI trade wobbled](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxPLWFfUWVYbDM3OXlSc2Zfcjg5THNXeDlYS21oVFF5MTJKMXhuemNtU3J0aVRPMVNtMEczeG5KdE5sbTNZdUFkZEF4eDNuNGFFc0huTmtuNWlFZ2JXN3BKd2lMRmJTMGMyREE4ODhXT3gzQmF1U1h5RWI4eWVmT3I1Z2lfZVhyS1JwTXRXZWRXUzl5Q1BJME1VWWlOV2dPQXl6RUY3dEhiNlROdU14SmwwZ2JHUE8zQQ?oc=5).

## AI and technology

The week's defining market move was a reversal in AI. The Philadelphia Semiconductor index [fell more than 11% over the week and the Nasdaq posted its worst week in four months](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMidkFVX3lxTE41bXo1dkNVbzY1VHRmd3VKV1ZUYkxhSmZ6cHhKNTJOOExPcmNIYmpiTm1JYW5vUlEwdEoxMjd2eWI4OWFmSW5wNk1uQUhWRTVDdnNvRV9aR25uN3BhNEVXekJhbEhMTGdneVBNc2xoNDFGemVBTWc?oc=5), with the sell-off blamed on [debt-fuelled data-centre spending fears](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxPOTU4NC1LQkVIWmxhbHl0VTdkM1g1dmlCZlR4eUFQLWpnZU9kQV9fQlZjQWdTWnVDVkJlcWpQY3pjUmk2R2t6a1lreFlkZkFYZnVib2VrOGtfbUozTUJhdDhMUERoS3RsbWllTlItOW1YWnRoVlZZb3FicnR1QkE5ZmJCR2tkcE9kdFliSms3Q2lpVzB1OS1uTXdTQmE3eTNBOGRyWllyRnNkekppT2xv?oc=5) and [Chinese competition](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMingFBVV95cUxNT1o2bHJ2OW9kVzUwaHpqMjdaaTNUeE0zVjA4Y01zSXR3ZzdaSFRYd3hIVGNYeWdxbm5PdWp1a2FiQk5fc2JPc0M2N3hEVzJUam5TM1V5VHpxWHFwNjlKaDlHS1RxVDFCaUxrVTdTMVRkd085SGhwdXhXRDNCWXdlakZnUlM3U1hsTl9qTlpfR2hvNlFlblhFRzg3cDFCdw?oc=5); The Economist noted [the AI industry's gigantic debts are making investors nervous](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqgFBVV95cUxOQjBPZ04tUnFocVdZQlM2dkF6N3hkVk9wTDB3SWVfbHo2ZFNvcnQtanBIX2JIVVg5UXpEZGVlRDIycFFmZmlUMHdjaFlwUzNOclNlUEdzaUtQMHNPY3FkdFZQUFIyclZCQURIN09YZHlWUUdmYkhYY3B6WDlEQ2ZqbEdaai1BNUQzX3VwNC02a01abVRPWmZwdWQyMUdjbzZiaHNDVmFuMWJhZw?oc=5). Treasuries rallied as [investors sought shelter from AI turbulence](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihAFBVV95cUxPYUozTHM0dkZqb01wNmhUc2twRnYzMk8yOTV5V2YwSW5ndGRjN0lwNDdNUGFWbHRrU0kwWEp4OGJUNXp4djlDQnE4eXNDdy1BVk1WTUNMV1RCUWtGN3FOcmx0NHFRRkRIY3IzYzEwandjV0FTNlRfbnNZbkxvbDMtNEgzWE4?oc=5). Separately, Anthropic said it will commit [5% of its shares to a "public benefit fund"](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiW0FVX3lxTE96d1pfMGRCUGNicWlMXzlMckdGTGlnMGJyM1ZwR3lxb2xoRG5BR19QaWNDVDBPVXFXRVhQd2lDM0RfTXNNMGE1WFgwNVR3R3MxQV9rV2lseGRSZ28?oc=5). By Monday, [Nasdaq futures were higher as some investors bought the dip](https://news.google.?oc=5).

## Company news and results

Bank earnings dominated the SEC filings. Bank of America [reported third-quarter net income of $6.9 billion and EPS of $0.91, against $8.3 billion and $1.04 a year earlier](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/70858/000007085826000481/bac09302026ex991.htm), with revenue up 3% to $30.0 billion and net interest income up 8% to $16.4 billion; results included a $1.2 billion regulatory settlement charge, and the bank said it returned $8.3 billion to shareholders. Average loans rose 6% year on year — useful evidence that credit is still flowing — while investment banking fees fell 11% and sales and trading revenue fell 5%. Reuters reported Wall Street banks were [caught in a capital markets lull after the first half](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwAFBVV95cUxNb29DeVJTNUVLRVV2LWFBdlBoTEMxOWdMWElmRTlGNm5HR2RXWUdobVdoZk55X3pqU1cwZUtpZno2RkZ3RU1TXzllSGc4emxJS3VMakU1ZkNLYWJLbDBUSF9kQkY5OENramlRZjVGbWVPckxsaGFzOU9sSnhMbWVUNk5uRGo4LU1BakdIZWZxZlZqcGl0QzFiMGdaT1QwWW1vLWh5VUtlUldiMmFxMENQMl9DNEx3YlZKeXlqSVRnUlI?oc=5).

Outside finance, Kimberly-Clark [published preliminary third-quarter data and kept its 2026 outlook consistent with previous expectations](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/55785/000110465926115960/tm2627599d1_ex99-1.htm), including adjusted operating profit growth in the mid single digits in constant currency; it flagged roughly 100 basis points of drag from previously disclosed China social media disruptions and said final results come on 5 November. More than 100 US companies filed quarterly results with the SEC during the week.

## Market mood

Nervous. The VIX — the options market's estimate of how much the S&P 500 will swing — rose almost 23% in a week to 18.69. CNN's Fear & Greed index sits at 20, "extreme fear", down from 46 a week ago and 30 a month ago. Yet credit markets were calm: the US high-yield spread (the extra interest riskier companies pay over the government) was 3.23 percentage points on 15 October, down slightly on the day. Gold was roughly flat at $4,185.30 and bitcoin at $82,137. On Reddit, mentions of broad index trackers roughly doubled in 24 hours alongside heavy chatter on memory and AI-infrastructure names — unverified opinion, but a reasonable gauge of where anxiety is concentrated.

## What to watch next week

UK September inflation lands midweek and [could seal the case for a November Bank of England rate hike](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiswFBVV95cUxPRFIxNENhNGRYUmJLQ0hiZW82dE4zSVVrTkp6ZExjbWk5djg5X1Fad0VIZVRGcVQ2R3ZySWZHOFZoTDZ3UWVXakdldk12T04tSWo5Z3pTR2JkMFpNRFhXTGtsbnRNZWdLRVR5QUItWnJnTGdXWVpaV2tUOG1IN3RGLTVRZHlXMkZlYldEc2JfR0h1NkhGejJfQk8ybVpZWHdmTVJmUzVVb28tYkdpMmNGM3VwRQ?oc=5); the ECB decides on 29 October; and the Fed meets with markets unusually unsure of the outcome. Oil and Gulf shipping remain the wildcard for prices and freight costs.
